title: GPU weeknote: priming, regional hedging, and small-batch experiments (2027-08-28)
content:
Context:
Quick sync for the infra team focused on short-term priming, a hedging proposal for low-demand regions, and the results from two small-batch experiments that ran last week. This is a working note — decisions below are proposals unless explicitly marked final.

Attendees:
- Aisha (notes/lead)
- Marcus (fleet ops)
- Lena (capacity forecasting)
- Samir (sre/runbooks)
- Priya (cost engineering)
- Ops oncall (joining for triage)

High-level status:
- Overall fleet steady. Tail latencies dipped Friday during a surge window but recovered after autoscaler bump. No customer-impacting outages.
- Short-term goal: reduce cold-start tail latency for hosted API by 20% during peak windows while keeping committed cost delta < 8%.

Regional snapshot (active pools as of 2027-08-28 07:00 UTC):
- us-west: 280 GPUs (H100x2-equivalent nodes), primed pool target 40%
- eu-west: 200 GPUs (mixed H100/L40S), primed pool target 30%
- apac-sg: 110 GPUs (L40S-heavy), primed pool target 20%
- sa-east: 42 GPUs (preemptible-heavy), primed pool target 10%
- af-south: 8 GPUs (edge trial), primed pool target 10%
Note: primed pool = warmed instances with KV cache snapshots and preloaded model variants.

Experiment summaries (small-batch runs):
1) "fast-warm" preloading (A/B across us-west 100-node subset)
- Approach: Keep a 10% node subset continuously warm for 2 models (chat-medium, embed-large). Rotate set every 6h to measure cache decay.
- Observations: P99 token latency improved ~18% for targeted routes. Cold-start QPS drop reduced by 35% for the warmed models.
- Cost: incremental GPU-hours +6% on tested subset; system-wide projected +2.8% if rolled out fleet-wide with selective model targeting.
- Risk: KV snapshot storage increased IOPS; we saw a transient SSE spike on snapshot writes during rotation windows.

2) "hedge-buckets" (regional hedging policy trial in eu-west & apac-sg)
- Approach: Create tiered capacity buckets (priority/hedge/overflow). Hedge bucket kept at 12% capacity and allowed preemption-friendly instances to backfill.
- Observations: During moderate surge, hedge buckets absorbed ~48% of overflow before invoking cross-region spill. Cross-region latencies stayed within SLO for 94% of requests.
- Cost: operationally cheaper than full always-on priming; preemption churn needs better retry smoothing.

Decisions and proposals:
- Roll forward with selective fast-warm for top 6 hosted models in us-west and eu-west. Target rollout: canary on 5% of traffic next week, then 20% by mid-September if metrics hold. Owner: Marcus.
- Adopt hedge-buckets as a region-level policy for low-demand regions (sa-east, af-south) with preemption-safe instances. Policy helm chart will be authored for autoscaler. Owner: Lena + Samir.
- Throttle KV snapshot rotations: increase rotation window from 6h -> 12h and add jitter to avoid IOPS spikes. Owner: Samir.

Action items (owner — due):
- Marcus: implement canary config for fast-warm in us-west (JIRA-OPS-1432). Due 2027-09-03.
- Lena: update capacity forecast incorporating fast-warm delta and hedge-bucket allocation; publish new forecast table. Due 2027-09-02.
- Priya: run cost model comparing full-priming vs hedge-bucket for next 6 months; include committed vs preemptible blended pricing. Due 2027-09-07.
- Samir: patch snapshot writer to add rate limits + jitter; run load test. Due 2027-09-01.
- Aisha: prepare customer-facing note for CS describing expected behavioral changes for enterprise dedicated clusters. Draft due 2027-09-06.

Open questions and concerns:
- How to safely migrate model variants between primed and baseline pools without causing cache thrash? (engineering investigation, Samir + Marcus).
- Can we automate eviction policies for hedge bucket preemptions to reduce user-visible retries? (design doc needed).
- Edge/af-south: is continued small footprint justified by latency-sensitive customers, or do we treat it as trial and rotate traffic to nearby regions? (product + infra callout)

Notes from SRE triage:
- Observed transient spike in snapshot write latency during rotation experiments (correlated with backup job). Proposed mitigation: stagger backups and snapshot rotations; probe writes with health check that temporarily disables rotation when IO > threshold.

Back-of-envelope capacity forecast (next 30 days, conservative):
- Expected baseline demand growth: +6% regionally (driven by new PLG promo and documentation indexing job).
- If we implement fast-warm (selective) and hedge-buckets: reserve delta ~ +3.5% GPU-hours overall; peak buffer target remains 12% to preserve SLOs.

Attach/refs:
- Priming playbook draft link in linked_artifacts.
- JIRA-OPS-1432 covers canary work.
- PR for snapshot writer rate limiter will land in github.com/redwood-infra/gpu-sim (linked above).

Summary/next meeting:
- Next sync: weekly check-in Tuesday 2027-09-01 09:00 UTC. Expect Marcus to present canary plan and Samir to present rotation patch results.
- If canary metrics (p99 latency, cold-start rate) show >12% improvement with cost delta <8%, proceed to 20% traffic rollout.

Quick sign-off: Aisha (lead) — draft until action items complete.
